subject: Post-call: StreamlinePay inference cost & ops constraints — next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@streamlinepay.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@streamlinepay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + proposed next steps from today's call

Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Solid conversation — I wanted to capture the highlights and make sure we're aligned on next steps. TL;DR: StreamlinePay is facing acute unit-cost pressure on inference (particularly for NLU and reranking flows); you're open to batching/caching and quantization but need pilot guardrails and a clear ops path.

Pain points we heard:
- Per-message token cost is up ~2.8x year-over-year; projections show ~3.5x spend growth if traffic increases 30%.
- Tight p95 latency target for UX-critical flows (~<200ms) but current endpoints (SageMaker-hosted LLMs) show 350–600ms p95 during peaks. Spiky QPS + short timeouts are causing user-facing errors.
- No prefix/KV cache in front of reranking; repeated prefixes are re-computed.
- Ops team lacks visibility into token-level costing and per-route traces (hard to prioritize optimization work).

Current stack (what you shared):
- Core inference on AWS (SageMaker endpoints using g4dn/p3), autoscaling based on CPU/instance counts; some request fan-out from a Node service.
- Logging aggregated to ELK, but no token-level billing exports today.
- Small internal evaluation of int8 quantized weights but not production-ready.

Success criteria you outlined:
- Reduce per-request inference cost by ~3x (or absolute monthly spend reduction of ~$Xk) while keeping p95 latency <=200ms for primary flows.
- No regression on LLM output quality beyond an agreed prompt-level eval set (we discussed a 1–2% drop ceiling on core metrics).
- Clear rollback/fallback path for canary/pilot (must not impact production SLAs).

What Redwood can do next (proposed):
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra + SRE (60–90m): perf profile of traffic, sample prompts, latency SLOs, current autoscaling triggers.
2) Pilot plan (4–6 weeks): scoped to two routes (conversation generation + reranking). We propose combining batching + prefix caching + int8 quantization candidate, instrumented with token-level cost dashboards.
3) Safety net: A/B canary with auto-fallback to current endpoints on quality/latency regressions.
4) Deliverables: mutual action plan (MAP), pilot runbook, expected cost/latency delta projection.

I've attached a brief playbook (PDF) and a starter MAP (Excel).

Next steps I propose:
- You: share sample prompt set + one week of anonymized tracing for the two routes (link or Drive upload).
- We: schedule the 60–90m technical deep-dive next week — suggested slots Tue/Wed 09:00–12:00 PT.
- Both: agree owner for the pilot runtime (we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private depending on compliance).

If that matches your view, I'll send a calendar invite for the deep-dive and kick off the MAP edit.

Thanks —
Monica

Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0186

Attachments: 20260912_redwood_cost_playbook.pdf (PDF), streamlinepay_map_v1.xlsx (Excel)
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@streamlinepay.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@streamlinepay.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed next steps from today's call

Thanks Monica — this is a great summary and captures the ask. A few clarifications from our side:
- The $Xk estimate you wrote above is roughly $45k/mo baseline today; our finance partner wants to see a path to ~60% reduction for the pilot routes to approve spend.
- We're comfortable with int8 experimentation but need to keep production quality checks; Alyssa will own the evaluation metrics and provide an eval harness.
- Deep-dive: Tue 09:30 PT works for us (I'll include our SRE lead, Priya).

Can you also include a short checklist of data we need sanitized for the pilot? We have strict PII rules and want to avoid back-and-forth.

Tom
Director of AI Engineering
StreamlinePay

On Tue, Sep 14, 2026 at 09:00 AM PDT Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Tom — noted. We'll aim for the 09:30 PT slot. I'll add a brief data-sanitization checklist to the MAP and flag the exact fields we need.

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@streamlinepay.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@streamlinepay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed next steps from today's call

Perfect — calendar invite sent for Tue 09:30 PT with a 75-minute block (deep-dive + quick ops sync).

Per Tom's ask I've attached a short data-sanitization checklist in the MAP and pasted the key items below:
- Sample prompts: pseudonymize any user identifiers, remove full account numbers, zero out tokens that look like payment card numbers.
- Traces: strip IP addresses and session ids; keep latency and token counts intact.
- Labels/ground-truth: provide a small labeled set for rerank eval (<=500 examples) with obfuscated user identifiers.

Karthik / Rishi — can you review the pilot guardrails below before the call?
- Pilot scope: 2 routes, 4–6 weeks, canary traffic 10–20% then ramp to 50% if no regressions.
- Objectives: cost delta projection, p95 latency target, and quality (A/B eval).
- Rollback: automatic fallback to current endpoints if quality delta > 2.5% absolute or p95 latency >250ms for two successive hours.

I'll bring an initial cost/latency projection to the call based on similar pilots.

Thanks —
Monica

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@streamlinepay.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@streamlinepay.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed next steps from today's call

Quick internal note:
- I'll prepare an ops checklist (autoscaling knobs, batching windows, cache TTL suggestions) and a short quantization risk note (quality vs speed tradeoffs) for the deep-dive.
- We should request a single representative prompt distribution file (JSON lines) with token counts so we can simulate batching benefits before the pilot.

Rishi — can you add any telemetry hooks we should require (token-level cost export, per-route traces)?

-- Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
